subject: Operations
title: Safety and Ergonomics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Safety and Ergonomics.

hook.text: In 1911, the Triangle Shirtwaist fire killed 146 workers. Locked exits turned a factory into a deathtrap.

buildup.text: Workplace safety protects people from injury. Ergonomics designs tasks to fit the human body.

discovery.text: Repetitive strain injuries cost US employers $20 billion a year. Better workstation design prevents them.

twist.text: Safety isn't just ethics—it's economics. Every injury means lost time, lawsuits, and lower morale.

climax.text: Alcoa's CEO made safety his top priority. Profits tripled because the culture of care improved everything.

punchline.text: Protect the people, and performance follows.

quiz.question: What happened when Alcoa's CEO prioritized safety above all else?
